name: Jeyuk Deopbap (Korean Spicy Pork Rice Bowl)
why: The classic Korean office-lunch bowl — thin-sliced pork seared in a garlicky, slightly sweet gochujang glaze, piled over rice in 35 minutes. A perfect one-pan weeknight dish that leans into your Korean cooking experiments.
author: Henry
ingredients: 1 lb thinly sliced pork shoulder or belly

steps: Whisk together the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, rice wine, minced garlic, and grated ginger into a marinade.
Toss the thinly sliced pork in the marinade and let it sit 15–20 minutes at room temperature — no longer, or the meat turns mushy.
Slice the onion and bell pepper. Steam the rice.
Heat the sesame oil in a wide pan or skillet over high heat until it's shimmering.
Add the onion and bell pepper and stir-fry for 1–2 minutes until just starting to soften.
Add the marinated pork in a single layer and let it sit undisturbed for a minute before stirring — this builds char and deep flavor.
Stir-fry until the pork is fully cooked and the sauce has thickened slightly, 5–7 minutes.
Pile the hot pork and vegetables over the steamed rice.
Serve with sliced cucumber alongside for a fresh, cooling contrast.

pro_tips: Don't skip the undisturbed minute — letting the pork sear before you stir is what gives it that smoky, charred restaurant flavor rather than just stewed-in-sauce.
Thin slicing matters more than the cut: if your pork isn't thin enough, lay it between cling film and freeze for 15 minutes, then slice — much easier and more even.
